sm: P. Andrew Sandlin argues that the gospel is political but not partisan. He says it is political by nature, since Jesus opened his ministry proclaiming the kingdom, and the gospel is the treaty of the great king offering pardon to rebels who trust him. It also bears on civil government, because politicians are bound by God's law and limited by it. He says it is not partisan, and the Bible opposes nationalism. He calls the recent election results tragic and criticizes the Democratic Party on abortion, sexuality and socialism. He also faults Republicans over abortion pills, tariffs, and antisemitic and racist voices, while praising some stands on transgenderism, Supreme Court nominees and border enforcement. He closes with Gideon and the angel asking whether you are on the Lord's side.
